request: Analyze GSE114062 for PMID 30071007 (Brain region-dependent gene networks associated with selective breeding for increased voluntary wheel-running behavior.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (Illumina HiSeq 2000, 100 nt PE), cerebellum and striatum, male Hsd:ICR mice, generation 66 of a selection experiment
final.primary_estimand: Associational difference in brain gene expression between a line selectively bred for high voluntary wheel running (Hi, line 7) and a non-selected control line (Co, line 1), within cerebellum (CeHi-CeCo) and striatum (StHi-StCo), plus the line-by-region interaction. All mice had 6 days of wheel access before sampling, so the contrast is genetic line (dominated by 66 generations of selection) with the running amount co-varying; it is not a randomized exercise intervention (S2.1.p3, S4.p3).
final.sample_inclusion: 16 samples (4 per line-region cell); one StHi sample removed as PCA outlier (S2.2.p1) -> 15 analysed; GEO deposits exactly these 15.
planned_contrasts: CeHi vs CeCo within cerebellum (S2.2.p2; Table 1/Table 3; reported as CeCo-CeHi)
StHi vs StCo within striatum (S2.2.p2; Table 1/Table 4; reported as StCo-StHi)
line-by-region interaction (S2.2.p2, S3.2.p1: 86 genes at FDR < 0.05; 334 at raw P < 0.005)
StHi vs CeHi (third orthogonal contrast, S2.2.p2; no count reported)
main effect of line Hi vs Co across regions (S2.2.p2, S3.6.p1; Table 5; 144 genes |log2FC|>1 in Table E, 122 genes after removing interaction genes; p rule not stated)
main effect of region St vs Ce (S2.2.p2, S3.7.p1; 243 genes at FDR < 1e-15 excluding interaction genes)
final.repeated_measure_unit: not stated by the authors; S2.2.p1 ('16 individual mouse samples'; 'half of the samples ... St and the rest ... Ce' within line) is compatible with 8 mice x 2 regions. Animal ID not deposited; candidate key = title suffix within line. Paper fits no animal term.
final.normalization: Cuffnorm v2.2.1 library-size normalized gene counts; genes with >= 1 CPM in >= 3 samples kept (15,213 genes); TMM (S2.2.p1)
final.paper_method: edgeR 3.14.0 GLM ~ line + region + line:region, robust tagwise dispersion, quasi-likelihood F-test, BH FDR (S2.2.p2)
final.paper_results: Interaction: 86 genes FDR < 0.05 (76 also FDR < 0.05 in a within-region line contrast); Table 1 top interaction genes; Table 5 top line main-effect genes; Tables 3-4 GSEA: oxidative phosphorylation and ribosome enriched among genes higher in Co than Hi in both regions

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Study map from S2.1.p1-p4 (design, 2x2 factorial, line 7 vs line 1, wheel access for all), S2.2.p1 (samples, filter, outlier removal), S2.2.p2 (edgeR QL model and contrasts), S3.2.p1 (FDR < 0.05 significance rule, 86 interaction genes), S3.6.p1/Table 5 (line main effect), S3.7.p1 (region effect). The paper's tables report Co minus Hi (log2(Co/Hi)); this run reports Hi vs Co, so signs are flipped when comparing.

15 GSM samples = 16 minus the removed StHi outlier (S2.2.p1): striatum Selected has 3 samples

ownership.reasoning: Accession named in the paper; organism, strain, sex, tissues, conditions and sample count match the paper's design after the documented outlier removal.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix column names equal the metadata title for all 15 samples (inspect alignment_keys: title 15/15). line and region are parsed from the title and agree with characteristics condition/tissue; recoded to the paper's labels Co/Hi and Ce/St. For the pairing sensitivity only: animal = title suffix within line (Control_0..3, Selected_0..3; candidate key, not deposited by the authors); hist = 1 for StHi cells (interaction indicator for the within-animal model); animal_ctrl pairs only Control samples by suffix and leaves every Selected sample as its own animal.

final.paper_input: Cuffnorm library-size-normalized gene counts, then TMM in edgeR (S2.2.p1)

matrix.reasoning: Despite the FPKM label, column sums are 38-44 million per sample (FPKM sums would not track fragment totals like this), and within each sample the non-zero values are integer multiples of one per-sample unit (e.g. 0.891534, 0.931986; 0.84-1.30, the mode value occurring ~900 times = one fragment): 81-96% of non-zero values are within 0.01 of an integer multiple, the rest are large values limited by 6-significant-digit printing. This is the Cuffnorm genes.count_table (counts scaled by geometric-mean size factors), which matches the paper's stated input (S2.2.p1 'Cuffnorm ... normalize the gene counts for library size'). Count-scale values on a near-unit scale are suitable for edgeR, which accepts non-integer counts; no rounding needed.

final.analysis_type: factorial 2x2 (line x region), one model on all 15 samples

design.reasoning: S2.1.p1 and S2.2.p1-p2 define a 2x2 factorial (activity line x brain region) fitted in one edgeR model with the interaction. The exercise-relevant estimand is Hi vs Co line within each region and the line-by-region interaction (S2.2.p2: 'patterns of particular interest'); the line main effect and the third orthogonal contrast StHi-CeHi plus the region main effect are secondary, as in the paper. The comparison is associational (selected line vs control line, both with wheel access; S2.1.p3, S4.p3), not a randomized exercise effect. Main effects are taken as averages over the other factor's levels because the model contains the interaction.

covariates.disposition: not in the primary model (paper fits none; animal ID not deposited; candidate key title suffix). Sensitivity only: edgeR QL with fixed animal (~ animal + region + hist) and voom with duplicateCorrelation block animal

covariates.disposition: excluded per paper (S2.2.p2): between-line variation dominates, no covariate

covariance.reasoning: All mice are male, same age and generation; no batch or RIN column in GEO. S2.2.p2 states no covariate was included. Whether cerebellum and striatum came from the same 8 mice is not stated (S2.2.p1 '16 individual mouse samples'); Animal ID not deposited; candidate key title suffix. The paper's model has no animal term, so the primary model has no blocking. Within-region line contrasts compare different animals either way; if regions were paired, region and interaction tests would be conservative-to-misestimated, which is recorded as a caveat. Data check (within-line residual Spearman correlation of log2 CPM between Ce and St samples over the 100-1000 genes most variable between animals): Control pairs by suffix are clearly supported (diagonal 0.29-0.58, off-diagonal <= 0.10 at top 100); Selected pairs by suffix are NOT supported (St_Sel_0 best matches Ce_Sel_3, St_Sel_1 matches Ce_Sel_0, only Sel_2 matches its suffix, and the pattern fades at 1000 genes). Pairing is therefore an assumption: supported by the data for Control and compatible with S2.2.p1, never stated by the authors. Run as labelled sensitivity analyses (suffix pairing in both lines = 7 pairs + unpaired CeHi Selected_3; and Control-only pairing); confirm with the authors or S1 File.

final.method: edgeR QL F-test (R edgeR glmQLFit/glmQLFTest, robust), TMM

method.reasoning: The paper's method (S2.2.p2) runs directly on the deposited count-scale matrix through tools.r_de_tools engine edger_ql (estimateDisp robust, glmQLFit robust, glmQLFTest per contrast, BH FDR). Contrasts are model-column vectors over ~ line * region with Co and Ce as references.

final.deviation_note: Audit rule raw P < 0.005 reproduces the paper's extended interaction list (Table A, 334 genes; S3.2.p1). Table 1 (FDR < 0.01, |log2FC| > 1.25), Table 5 (FDR < 0.01, |log2FC| > 4) and Table 6 are display filters, not DEG definitions.

threshold.reasoning: S3.2.p1: significance is 'FDR-adjusted P-value < 0.05' (86 interaction genes); no fold-change rule in the DEG definition.

caveats: Associational: selected high-runner line vs control line, both given 6 days of wheel access; differences reflect genetic selection plus differing running amounts and cannot be read as an effect of exercise per se (S4.p3).

Direction conflict with the paper's text: our Hi-vs-Co log2FC within region equals the paper's Table 1 'CeCo-CeHi'/'StCo-StHi' values with the SAME sign (Npsr1 Ce -6.47, Vdr -3.37, Pcsk9 +3.21, Krt25 Ce -1.98 / St +3.02, Cd300lf St -4.23), so Table 1 columns are numerically Hi minus Co under the GEO Control/Selected labels. The paper's text reads them as Co minus Hi and therefore states the opposite direction: e.g. it says Npsr1, Vdr, Necab1 and Cd300lf are over-expressed in Hi and Npy/Pcsk9 under-expressed in Hi (S3.2.p3-p6), whereas the data show Npsr1/Vdr/Necab1/Cd300lf lower and Npy/Pcsk9 higher in Selected; Spp1 is higher (not lower) in St of Selected (S3.5.p2).

Table 5 (log2(Co/Hi)) agrees in sign with the data (Ms4a2 Co/Hi +8.20 = our Hi-vs-Co -8.20; Cyp11a1 higher in Hi as the text says), so the GEO line labels appear correct and the Table 1 header/text sign is the paper's inconsistency.

GSEA (Hallmark here, GO/KEGG in the paper): oxidative phosphorylation is enriched among genes HIGHER in the Selected line in both regions (NES +2.23 Ce, +1.76 St); the paper's text says oxidative phosphorylation is over-expressed in Co relative to Hi (S3.4.p3). Same sign problem as Table 1; recorded, not resolved.

Animal ID not deposited; candidate key title suffix. If Ce and St came from the same mice, the primary region and interaction tests ignore that pairing (as the paper did). Pairing sensitivity (edgeR fixed animal; voom duplicateCorrelation) is reported separately; the suffix pairing is supported by the data for Control but not for Selected samples, and is an assumption not stated by the authors (ask the authors / check S1 File).
edgeR 4.x QL defaults differ from edgeR 3.14; counts are not expected to match exactly.

study.reasoning: Paper's model, test, filter and threshold reproduced on the deposited matrix; only the interaction has a paper count under the FDR < 0.05 rule. Within-region line counts are only in S1 Figure A (not available); line main-effect counts (144/122) use an unstated p rule with |log2FC| > 1.
